claims.text: Correlations between symptoms of addictive technology use and mental disorder symptoms were all positive and significant.
The interrelationship between addictive use of social media and addictive use of video games is weak.
Age is inversely related to the addictive use of social media and video games.
Being male is significantly associated with addictive use of video games.
Being female is significantly associated with addictive use of social media.
Being single is positively related to addictive social networking.
Being single is positively related to addictive video gaming.
Demographic factors explain between 11% and 12% of the variance in addictive technology use.
Mental health variables explain between 7% and 15% of the variance in addictive technology use.
The concept of Internet use disorder as a unified construct is not warranted.

evidence.description: Correlations between symptoms of addictive technology use and mental disorder symptoms were all positive and significant.
Results showed a weak interrelationship between the two addictive technological behaviors.
Age appeared to be inversely related to the addictive use of these technologies.
Being male was significantly associated with addictive use of video games.
Being female was significantly associated with addictive use of social media.
Being single was positively related to both addictive social networking and video gaming.
Being single was positively related to both addictive social networking and video gaming.
Hierarchical regression analyses showed that demographic factors explained between 11 and 12% of the variance in addictive technology use.
The mental health variables explained between 7 and 15% of the variance.
The study suggests that the concept of Internet use disorder (i.e., "Internet addiction") as a unified construct is not warranted.

methodologies.name: Cross-sectional online survey and hierarchical regression analysis
methodologies.description: An online cross-sectional survey of adults evaluating demographic factors and psychiatric symptoms as predictors of addictive social media and video game use using hierarchical regression.
